record_title: The Euclidean Jung constant is the universal local Hausdorff–Gromov–Hausdorff constant
limitations: Originality is to the best of our knowledge. The optimal second-order coefficient is not identified; deleted geodesic balls are not proved exactly optimal on curved manifolds; no classification of all asymptotically extremizing subsets is claimed. The result is restricted to smooth closed Riemannian manifolds of dimension at least two. The key lower estimate is a scale optimization of a published comparison theorem, so differently phrased or not-yet-indexed related observations remain a residual originality risk.
